transcript.text:
Sorry to hear that! Here are the most common causes, roughly from easiest to hardest to fix:

## 1. Quick checks first
• Unbalanced load: Machines often refuse to spin (or keep trying and stopping) if clothes are bunched on one side. A single heavy item like a towel, rug, or jeans is a classic cause. Redistribute or add/remove items and try a spin-only cycle.
• Overloaded drum: Take some clothes out and retry.
• Spin setting: Make sure "No Spin," "Rinse Hold," or a very low spin speed isn't selected.
• Restart it: Unplug for 5 to 10 minutes, then plug back in and run a Spin or Rinse & Spin cycle.

## 2. Is there water left in the drum?
If yes, it's probably a drainage problem. Most machines won't spin until the water is gone.
• Clean the pump filter (front loaders): Usually behind a small flap at the bottom front. Put towels and a shallow tray down first, because water will come out. Look for coins, hair grips, socks, or lint.
• Check the drain hose: Make sure it isn't kinked, squashed behind the machine, or blocked.
• Listen during drain: A humming pump with no water moving suggests a blockage. Silence could mean a faulty pump.

## 3. Door / lid lock
• The machine won't spin if it doesn't detect the door as locked. Make sure the door shuts firmly and nothing is caught in the seal.
• If the door lock light doesn't come on or blinks, the door lock/lid switch may be faulty (a fairly cheap part).

## 4. Mechanical issues (if the above doesn't work)
• Drive belt (common in older/budget machines): With the machine unplugged, try turning the drum by hand. If the motor runs or hums but the drum doesn't turn, the belt may be broken or slipped.
• Motor carbon brushes or a motor/control board fault: Usually a job for a technician.

## 5. Check for an error code
If your display shows a code (e.g. E21, F05, UE, OE), tell me. It often points straight to the problem.

---

To help further, could you tell me:
1. Make and model (e.g. Samsung, LG, Bosch, Beko, Whirlpool)?
2. Front loader or top loader?
3. Is water left in the drum?
4. Any error code, beeping, or humming noise?

⚠️ Always unplug the machine before opening panels, checking the belt, or reaching inside.
its a hotpoint, front loader. no water left in the drum, no error code. it just finished the wash and the bath mat was dripping wet, drum kept sloshing and trying to speed up then slowing down

That's almost certainly an unbalanced load. A single bath mat is one of the worst offenders. When it's soaked it becomes one heavy lump, so the machine senses the imbalance, slows down, tumbles back and forth to try to redistribute it, then tries again. That's the "speed up, slow down" cycle you saw. It's a safety feature, not a fault.

## Fix it now
1. Add a few towels (2 to 3 bath towels) so the weight spreads more evenly around the drum.
2. Select Rinse & Spin or Spin only and run it.
3. If you'd rather not add anything, take the mat out, wring out what you can, put it back spread around the drum (not bunched), and spin again on a lower spin speed (e.g. 800 rpm).

## Worth knowing
• Rubber-backed mats: Hotpoint (and most manufacturers) advise against washing these in the machine. The backing can break up and clog the filter or pump, and they're very hard to balance. If yours is rubber-backed, check the pump filter (bottom front flap) for bits of rubber, and consider hand-washing it in future.
• Next time, wash mats with towels, not on their own.

## If a balanced, normal load still won't spin
Then it may be something else:
• Machine not level: Check that it doesn't rock and adjust the feet.
• Worn shock absorbers/suspension: Look for excessive banging or the drum sagging.
• Worn motor carbon brushes: These are common on older Hotpoints. The drum turns slowly but won't reach full speed.

Try the towels first. I'd bet that sorts it. Let me know how it goes!
ok will try it with a couple of towels and a rinse & spin. the mat is rubber backed yeah, its the big heavy one from the dog

Sounds like a good plan. A heavy, rubber-backed dog mat is about as tricky as it gets, so the towels should help a lot.

## A couple of things since it's rubber-backed and from the dog
• Check the pump filter afterwards. Dog hair plus bits of rubber backing are a common cause of drain blockages. Put towels and a shallow tray down, open the flap at the bottom front, and slowly unscrew the filter.
• If it still struggles, drop the spin speed to 800 rpm or lower. Heavy rubber mats don't need a fast spin, and it's gentler on the machine and the mat.
• Check the mat itself. If the backing is cracking or flaking, it's probably time to stop machine-washing it.

## For next time
• Shake or vacuum it first to get rid of loose hair and grit.
• Hand wash or hose it down outside and let it air dry, or
• Consider a machine-washable dog mat without rubber backing (lots are designed for this).
• Run an empty hot wash (60 °C or a drum clean cycle) now and then to clear dog hair from the drum and seal.

Hopefully the rinse & spin does the trick. Shout if it still won't spin properly!
ok did the rinse & spin with the mat and a couple of towels. it spun up fine this time and the mat came out damp not dripping

Great news, glad that sorted it! 🎉 It was just the unbalanced load, so nothing's wrong with your machine.

## Just a couple of quick things
• Dry the mat flat or hang it up, rather than tumble drying. Heat breaks down rubber backing quickly.
• Check the pump filter when you get a chance, since dog hair and rubber bits from that wash may have collected in there.

In future, washing it with a few towels (or hosing it down outside) should save you the hassle. Shout if you need anything else!
